pins.name: D4
pins.label: D4 (Button)
pins.notes: Left button (Button A). Confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (Adafruit_Circuit_Playground.h: `#define CPLAY_LEFTBUTTON 4` in the __AVR__ block) and the official "Introducing Circuit Playground" pinout guide. This physical pin is also aliased as "A6" (value 24) elsewhere in this same pins_arduino.h -- see the "24" entry below, tagged identically.

pins.name: D5
pins.label: D5
pins.notes: Dedicated to the onboard piezo speaker/buzzer -- confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_BUZZER 5`; `pinMode(CPLAY_BUZZER, OUTPUT)` in begin()) and the official pinout guide ("D5 - Speaker PWM output"). Not general purpose.

pins.name: D7
pins.label: D7
pins.notes: Dedicated interrupt line from the onboard LIS3DH accelerometer -- confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_LIS3DH_INTERRUPT 7`) and the official pinout guide ("D7 - Accelerometer interrupt"). Not general purpose.

pins.name: D8
pins.label: D8
pins.notes: Chip-select line for the onboard LIS3DH accelerometer, which on this board (the 'classic'/AVR variant only) is wired over dedicated hardware SPI, NOT I2C -- confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_LIS3DH_CS 8`; `lis = Adafruit_CPlay_LIS3DH(CPLAY_LIS3DH_CS, &SPI); // SPI` in begin(), __AVR__ branch only). This physical pin is also aliased as "A8" (value 26) elsewhere in this pins_arduino.h -- see the "26" entry below, tagged identically. Not general purpose.

pins.name: D13
pins.label: D13 (Led active high)
pins.notes: Onboard small red status LED, active-high. Confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_REDLED 13`; `redLED(bool v)` calls `digitalWrite(CPLAY_REDLED, v)`, and Adafruit's own "Basic LEDs" lesson states writing it HIGH turns the LED on) and the official pinout guide ("D13 - Red LED"). Supports PWM per this file's own digitalPinHasPWM() macro (TIMER4A).

pins.name: D14
pins.label: D14
pins.notes: Hardware SPI MISO, entirely dedicated to the onboard LIS3DH accelerometer's private SPI bus on this board (see "8" above) -- no other onboard or user-facing device shares this bus. Not general purpose.

pins.name: D15
pins.label: D15
pins.notes: Hardware SPI SCK, entirely dedicated to the onboard LIS3DH accelerometer's private SPI bus on this board (see "8" above). Not general purpose.

pins.name: D16
pins.label: D16
pins.notes: Hardware SPI MOSI, entirely dedicated to the onboard LIS3DH accelerometer's private SPI bus on this board (see "8" above). Not general purpose.

pins.name: D17
pins.label: D17 (Led Neopixel)
pins.notes: Data pin for the ring of 10 onboard mini NeoPixels (WS2812-style). Confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_NEOPIXELPIN 17`; `strip.setPin(CPLAY_NEOPIXELPIN)`) and the official pinout guide ("D17 - Built-in 10 NeoPixels"). This pin is also this board's hardware SPI SS line (pins_arduino.h: `static const uint8_t SS = 17;`) -- not a conflict since the entire hardware SPI bus (D14/D15/D16 plus this SS line) is already fully dedicated to the onboard accelerometer (see "14"/"15"/"16"/"8" below), so SS is never needed for a real SPI transaction; the override here deliberately omits any spi_ss tag (avoids the identity/bus-tag contamination bug class documented in the pin-audit playbook section 12).

pins.name: D18
pins.label: D18
pins.notes: Dedicated to the onboard NTC thermistor (temperature sensor) -- confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_THERMISTORPIN A0` = digital pin 18) and the official pinout guide ("A0 - Temperature Sensor"). Not general purpose.

pins.name: D19
pins.label: D19 (Button)
pins.notes: Right button (Button B). Confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_RIGHTBUTTON 19`) and the official pinout guide.

pins.name: D22
pins.label: D22
pins.notes: Dedicated to the onboard microphone (analog sound sensor) -- confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_SOUNDSENSOR A4` = digital pin 22) and the official pinout guide ("A4 - Microphone sound sensor"). Not general purpose.

pins.name: D23
pins.label: D23
pins.notes: Dedicated to the onboard phototransistor (light sensor) -- confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_LIGHTSENSOR A5` = digital pin 23) and the official pinout guide ("A5 - Light Sensor"). Not general purpose.

pins.name: D24
pins.label: D24 (Button)
pins.notes: Same physical pin as D4 (left Button A) -- pins_arduino.h aliases it a second time as A6 (static const uint8_t A6 = 24; // D4). Tagged identically to "4" so this duplicate index doesn't appear as an ordinary free pin (see the parser-gotcha comment above the chipGpios block).

pins.name: D26
pins.label: D26
pins.notes: Same physical pin as D8 (accelerometer chip-select) -- pins_arduino.h aliases it a second time as A8 (static const uint8_t A8 = 26; // D8). Tagged identically to "8" so this duplicate index doesn't appear as an ordinary free pin (see the parser-gotcha comment above the chipGpios block).

pins.name: D30
pins.label: D30
pins.notes: Internal 'send' reference pin shared by the onboard capacitive-touch-sensing circuit for all 8 general-purpose alligator pads (D0/D1/D2/D3/D6/D9/D10/D12) -- confirmed via the official Adafruit_CircuitPlayground library (`#define CPLAY_CAPSENSE_SHARED 30`; driven as `pinMode(CPLAY_CAPSENSE_SHARED, OUTPUT)` and passed as the common send-pin to all 8 `CPlay_CapacitiveSensor(CPLAY_CAPSENSE_SHARED, <pad>)` instances in begin()). Not a user-facing alligator pad at all (absent from Adafruit's own pinout guide's pad list) and driving/reading it independently would disrupt touch sensing on every pad. Not general purpose.
